Gratuitous

/gruh-TOO-ih-tuhs/ - the stress falls on TOO · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Gratuitous means uncalled for, unwarranted.

The referee let the hard tackle go but flagged the gratuitous shove that came three seconds after the whistle.

Worked Example

The best man's toast ran warm and funny for four minutes. Then came the crack about the groom's old girlfriend — unasked for, connected to nothing, answered by the loudest silence a banquet hall can hold. He had the room; the jab bought him nothing and cost him most of it.

Gratuitous is precise because the line had no cause and no purpose: nothing invited it, no joke needed it, no point was served. Harsh words can be earned — a review can owe its subject some pain. A gratuitous jab is the kind nothing owed.

How Gratuitous Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

unprovoked

unprovoked: nothing invited it — said of attacks and insults

needless

needless: serving no purpose a need could explain

Antonyms

justified

justified: backed by good reason

deserved

deserved: earned by the receiver's own actions

How Strong Is It? — unasked-for → gratuitous → spiteful

unasked-for vs. gratuitous

unasked-for vs. gratuitous: Unasked-for advice merely arrives without an invitation; a gratuitous remark goes further — nothing invited it and nothing is served by it.

spiteful vs. gratuitous

spiteful vs. gratuitous: Spiteful passes gratuitous on the ladder: the uncalled-for remark now has a motive, and the motive is to wound.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — gratuit-

Root — gratuit-: freely given, unearned (from Latin gratus, pleasing, thankful)

Suffix — -ous

Suffix — -ous: of the nature of

Put it together

Put it together: Gratuit- (freely given — from Latin gratus, 'pleasing, thankful') + -ous = given free. A gratuity is money handed over that no bill demanded; gratuitous keeps that logic and sours it: something delivered that nothing demanded — most often an insult, a shove, or a scene a story didn't need.

Use the root in a new word: gratitude

Root Check

Word Choice

formal, disapproving

Gratuitous faults a thing for its cause: nothing called for it. Frivolous, its unit-mate, faults a thing for its weight: too light for the moment. A frivolous question wastes the panel's time; a gratuitous insult had no business existing. When reviewers flag gratuitous scenes, they mean the story owed us none of that.
